q: When water is released immediately from the main, what system can be used to supply higher levels?
n: Per the MST key, a deluge system.

q: What pipe supplies each floor with water for firefighting?
n: Standpipes feed hose valves on each floor.

q: What is the maximum height of a Siamese connection from the ground line?
n: Fire department connections sit between about 450 mm and 1200 mm above grade.

q: What is a Siamese (fire department) connection for?
o: Letting fire trucks pump water into the standpipe or sprinkler system
n: The FDC lets the fire service boost the system.

q: Which system is set off by heat and discharges only at the heads that open?
n: In a wet system water is already at each head.

q: Which pump is used to eject sewage or liquid waste?
n: A sump (ejector-type) pump lifts sewage or liquid waste to the sewer.

q: Which pump removes water from the lowest part of a building?
n: Sump pumps drain pits and basements.

q: What is the best location for installing a water pump?
n: Per the MST answer key: Cistern.

q: Where is a pump ideally located in relation to a cistern?
o: Side by side with the cistern
n: Per the MST answer key: On top of the cistern.

q: Which pump keeps adequate pressure on the upper floors of a multi-story building?
n: Boosters make up static head losses.

q: Considering the operational needs and potential emergency scenarios in a three-storey hospital, how many elevators are recommended to serve both patients and staff?
o: One, but it is ideal to have one for passengers
One for passengers and one for patients on stretchers
n: A hospital needs a passenger elevator plus a stretcher-size elevator for patients.

q: Given the building height and expected load of a three-storey hospital, which type of elevator system is most appropriate for efficient and safe vertical transportation?
n: Per the MST answer key: Traction or hydraulic.

q: In the design of a three-storey hospital, which of the following fire suppression systems is typically NOT included in standard fire safety protocols?
n: Per the MST key, a dry standpipe (not needed in a low-rise building).

q: According to fire code requirements, how many dry standpipes are typically required in a three-storey hospital?
n: Dry standpipes are required only from four storeys up, so none for three storeys.

q: What is the most appropriate and code-compliant location for installing a dry standpipe in a hospital?
n: Standpipe outlets go in the exit stairways, where firefighters stage.

q: Which of these does NOT make elevators?
o: None of the above — all three do
n: All three build elevators.

q: Which brand is well known for its ultra-fast elevators used in skyscrapers?
n: Per the MST answer key: Mitsubishi.

q: Which elevator brand is from Finland?
n: KONE is Finnish.

q: Which is one of the oldest elevator makers, founded in the United States?
n: Elisha Otis demonstrated the safety brake in 1854.

q: Which German company makes elevators and escalators worldwide?
n: Schindler is Swiss and KONE Finnish.

q: Which of these makes elevators and escalators?
n: KONE is a lift maker.

q: After how many minutes of inactivity will an escalator temporarily stop to save electricity?
n: Escalators on auto-stop typically pause after about three minutes with no passengers.

q: What is the minimum load capacity of a home elevator in kilograms?
n: Per the MST answer key: 250 kg.

q: What do you call the door inside the elevator?
n: The door on the car itself is the cab (car) door.

q: Which part opens and closes elevator doors automatically?
n: The operator is mounted on the car top.

q: Which is NOT a fire protection device?
n: Per the answer key, a firewall is a fire-rated building element, not a device.

q: What device senses smoke and triggers an alarm?
n: Smoke detectors sense particles.

q: Which part discharges water automatically when it senses heat?
n: A fusible link or glass bulb opens the head.

q: Which equipment is used to put out small fires by hand?
n: Portable extinguishers are for incipient fires.
